record.reason: Independently re-reviewed clean HEAD 8cbc30d (worktree clean; agent/next.md still P20.3 READY_TO_RUN, agent/staged/P20.3.md and P20.4.md still PENDING DESIGN, no lifecycle/roadmap mutation; compileall clean; graphify index refreshed 14:43:08 before the 14:43:30 commit). The three prior blocking findings are genuinely closed at this HEAD: (1) cumulative_remediation_rounds > max_plan_remediation_rounds now records a durable OwnerControlStore gate and _finish(owner_gate), which is outside _ACTIVE_STATES, so the planner lifecycle is no longer wedged (reproduced: RED evidence shows 'planning', GREEN shows 'owner_gate' plus is_paused); (2) ReviewRunner now publishes active-review-dispatch.json with the real per-packet broker request_id and DefaultReviewerHarness.status correlates it with AIBrokerExecutionPort.status()'s resource_id, persisting a parent_session_id-linked row that cleanup_timed_out passes to cleanup_stale_role_tool_children, and the production timeout path additionally records a deterministic durable gate — the call sites are no longer dead by construction; graphify read-only detection now checks the actual subcommand (argv[tool_index+1]) and persist_harness_session no longer rewrites unchanged rows; (3) reserve_recovery_attempt now binds effect_id=command_id with effect_kind=control_continue before submit_control_command, so a crash between publish and settlement reconciles via cmd_store.get(command_id) instead of being permanently rejected as 'unbound resource recovery command'. Evidence reproduces on this HEAD: the seven P20.3 suites = 77 passed; the regression set (ai_planner, ai_reviewer, control_commands, watchdog_recovery, watchdog, p145_reviewer_harness, p14_durable_jobs, planning_convergence_recovery) = 188 passed, 22 subtests; full tests_py = 1878 passed, 130 subtests, with only two pre-existing/environmental failures unrelated to this task (test_p16 SID detection; test_p17 convergence-import boundary, whose offending import in incidents/replay_runner.py dates from P20.2 commit 9143e8e). The task is nevertheless not complete: the single production recovery actuation path has no outcome reconciliation, so every non-accepted command outcome is a silent, permanent, non-owner-visible stall — CONFIRMED by direct reproduction, not inference. (a) When ControlCommandCoordinator blocks the wd-plan continue command (including via P20.3's own new 'unbound resource recovery command' / 'invalid selected recovery resource' / 'selected recovery resource no longer available' rejections added in ac2cf32), the control history records state=blocked while the watchdog problem stays state=retrying with attempt state=requested; every later tick returns planning_recovery_already_reserved, no owner gate is recorded, the project is not paused, and reconcile_recovery_attempts marks the ledger attempt 'reconciled: bound_to_existing_control_command' — reporting convergence for a rejected effect. (b) A handled enqueue failure leaves problem=blocked and attempt=blocked with ledger status=failed; the failed_plan_id dedup still answers planning_recovery_already_reserved after a fresh WatchdogCoordinator load (restart), with no gate and no retry. (c) A crash between reserve and submit leaves the ledger attempt reserved and, after TTL, abandoned ('effect_proven_absent') while the same dedup blocks any new attempt. _reconcile_recoveries (watchdog.py:1374-1430) already implements exactly the needed pattern — including the 'command was reserved but never enqueued before crash' -> unresolved + OWNER_GATE milestone — for prow['attempts'], recovery_slots and execution_loss_slots, but planning_recovery_problems[*]['attempts'] is covered by nothing. This violates the declared convergence evidence ('all CPF faults converge without manual continuation') and the fail-closed checklist item (it refuses but does not gate) on the watchdog_recovery boundary for CPF-03/CPF-07. Both fixes are local and bounded; no design reopening and no owner input is required. Non-blocking notes that must not consume a further round: DefaultReviewerHarness.status() re-probes execution_port.status() on every poll until a resource_id appears (with the local transport each probe spawns an ai_resource_broker.cli subprocess that can block up to 60s, unlike diagnostics.py:262-279 which deliberately deadline-bounds the same call), and load_aibroker_execution_port() sits outside that try so a malformed aibroker-execution.json would fail every harness review — latent today because no project in config/projects.json sets reviewer_harness.enabled; cleanup_timed_out can only ever terminate registered graphify children and nothing in the tree registers any, so it is fail-closed-but-inert and the new timeout gate carries the actionable outcome; restart_recovery_cycle is still permanently False, leaving the while True wrapper and max_plan_recovery_cycles affecting only message text.

qualification: REMEDIATE; not authoritative acceptance or soak
